protect_summary: 7 Protects in two attempts, 5 with a real payoff (4 blocked KOs, 1 blocked a heavy hit) and 2 empty (Kyogre T2 both times). No consecutive-Protect attempts and no Fini Protect spam this time (Fini Protected once in a1, was Encored in a2). Cadence is much healthier than build-9's.

ai_defects.description: Second authored Mega never fires once the first has been used. a2: Starmie sat on the field for four turns (T14 Liquidation, T15 Protect, T16 Aqua Jet, T17 Aqua Jet) with usable_gimmick=mega reported every turn and never Mega Evolved; a1: same on its single turn. Build-9 a2 proved Starmie does Mega when Milotic dies un-evolved, so the block is the one-Mega-per-trainer path, not Starmie's set.

Kyogre at full HP under rain chose Origin Pulse over Water Spout on T1 in both attempts (it was Fake Out flinched both times so the choice cost nothing here). Water Spout was chosen on T3 at 58-70% HP, when Origin Pulse would have been the stronger move; the selection looks inverted relative to HP.
Kyogre Protect T2 both attempts at 58-70% HP with nothing aimed at it - an empty Protect on a repeatable cadence (T2 after being Fake Out flinched T1). Consistent with build-9's a2/a3.
No switch-ins into super-effective attacks this time: the AI made no voluntary switches in either attempt (build-13's switch-in charging fix or simply no trigger).
No consecutive Protects and no Fini Protect spam; every Ferrothorn/Fini/Starmie Protect except Kyogre's T2 blocked a real hit.

calibration: Won 6-2 on the first attempt (two faints, one of them the Kingambit trade into the Milotic/Ferrothorn core) and 6-4 on the second (Milotic's Recover loop plus my Iron Bundle misplay). Both were real fights: keep all offsets (seeds 96/100/100/96/98/97 -> medium 94/98/98/94/96/95).
driver_notes: damage/faints in this build's act output are keyed by slot (opponent_a:<slot>, player:<slot>), not by species; the battle-ending turn carries no native choices, so Starmie's move on a1's last turn is unknown.
cooler: Unchanged from receipt.json: the room is the campaign's most tactically alive (Protect reads, the Recover loop, Aqua Jet beating priority). It would be cooler still with the second Mega actually firing and Water Spout opening at full HP.
legality: No legality problem found in the authored set.
verdict: Wallace is still the hardest fight of the League on build-13, but by a narrower margin than on build-9: with the party that beat Drake first try it now falls in one attempt with two faints, and the second attempt cost four. Its difficulty comes from decision density (Protect timing, Milotic's Recover, Ferrothorn's seed attrition) rather than raw damage, and it is being held back by the un-firing Mega Starmie; with defect 1 fixed the Huge Power Starmie in the back would make it clearly the summit.
